title: Python for Backend & Systems
tagline: Pythonic architecture, async concurrency, type hinting, and modern production APIs
description: From Python data structures and generator mechanics to asyncio event loops, FastAPI microservices, Pydantic data validation, and GIL concurrency tradeoffs.

stages.title: Stage 1: Pythonic Idioms & Data Structures
stages.description: List comprehensions, generators, dunder methods, decorators, and context managers.

nodes.title: Generators, Iterators & Custom Decorators
nodes.description: Lazy evaluation with `yield`, implementing `__iter__` and `__next__`, creating higher-order function decorators, and `functools.wraps`.
nodes.whyItMatters: Loading 10GB CSV files into memory crashes the server. Generators process streams row-by-row in constant O(1) memory space.

resources.title: Real Python: Primer on Python Decorators

keyTakeaways: Generators evaluate lazily on-demand, saving vast amounts of RAM when streaming large datasets.
Decorators wrap functions to add cross-cutting concerns (logging, timing, auth) without mutating the target function.
Use contextlib.contextmanager for clean resource management (database connections, file locks).
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers often ask you to write a retry decorator with exponential backoff or implement an infinite Fibonacci generator.

stages.title: Stage 2: Concurrency & The GIL
stages.description: Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), threading vs multiprocessing, and asynchronous I/O with asyncio.

nodes.title: asyncio, ThreadPoolExecutor & Multi-Processing
nodes.description: How Python handles I/O-bound tasks with cooperative multitasking (`async`/`await`) vs CPU-bound tasks with `multiprocessing.Process`.
nodes.whyItMatters: Because of Python's GIL, multithreading cannot speed up CPU-heavy tasks. Understanding when to use asyncio vs multiprocessing prevents performance bottlenecks.

resources.title: Real Python: Speed Up Your Python Program With Concurrency

keyTakeaways: Use asyncio for high-concurrency I/O operations (HTTP APIs, database calls).
Use multiprocessing to bypass the GIL and utilize multiple CPU cores for heavy mathematical calculations.
Never execute blocking synchronous calls (like `time.sleep` or synchronous requests) inside an async event loop.
nodes.interviewTips: Explain why the GIL exists, what changed with free-threaded Python 3.13, and how asyncio differs from OS threads.

stages.title: Stage 3: Production Web APIs with FastAPI
stages.description: FastAPI framework, Pydantic type validation, dependency injection, and SQLAlchemy 2.0 async ORM.

nodes.title: FastAPI Architecture, Pydantic & Async DB
nodes.description: Building production REST APIs with automatic OpenAPI schema generation, request payload validation, and connection pooling.
nodes.whyItMatters: FastAPI is among the fastest Python web frameworks, offering automated documentation and type-enforced safety that catches invalid API requests early.
keyTakeaways: Leverage FastAPI's `Depends` system for modular database session lifecycle and authentication token extraction.
Use Pydantic models for both request validation and response serialization filtering.
Deploy with ASGI servers like Uvicorn behind Gunicorn process managers.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to design a token-authenticated endpoint with database connection injection and custom error handling.
